user_query: What are my legal rights if the police stop or arrest me in India?
legal_text_raw: Under Section 47 BNSS, every person arrested without warrant has the right to be informed of full grounds of arrest and right to bail. Section 53 BNSS mandates medical examination by a medical officer within 48 hours. Supreme Court in D.K. Basu established strict arrest guidelines.
layman_explanation:
Under BNSS 2023 and the landmark D.K. Basu judgment, citizens have 4 fundamental arrest protections:
• Right to Know Grounds: The police officer must wear clear identification and immediately inform you of the exact offence and whether it is bailable.
• Right to Inform Family: You have the right to have a relative or friend informed of your arrest and location immediately.
• Right to Legal Counsel & Medical Exam: You can consult an advocate of your choice during interrogation and undergo mandatory medical examination within 48 hours.
• Presentation within 24 Hours: Police must produce you before the nearest Magistrate within 24 hours (excluding travel time).

user_query: The local police station is refusing to file an FIR because the crime happened outside their area. What is a Zero FIR?
legal_text_raw: Section 173 BNSS codifies Zero FIR provisions. Information relating to commission of a cognizable offence can be registered irrespective of the territorial jurisdiction of the police station, numbered as '0' and subsequently transferred to the competent jurisdiction police station.
layman_explanation:
Police CANNOT refuse to register an FIR based on territorial jurisdiction:
• A 'Zero FIR' allows any police station in India to register a cognizable crime report regardless of where the incident occurred.
• The station registers the complaint under number '0', initiates initial investigation/medical examination, and transfers it to the proper police station.
• If police refuse, escalate in writing to the Superintendent of Police under Section 173(4) BNSS or approach the Judicial Magistrate under Section 175(3) BNSS.

user_query: I have apprehension that my business rival might file a false criminal complaint against me. Can I apply for Anticipatory Bail?
legal_text_raw: Section 482 BNSS empowers the High Court and Court of Session to grant anticipatory bail to any person who has reason to believe that they may be arrested on accusation of having committed a non-bailable offence.
layman_explanation:
Yes, you can apply for 'Anticipatory Bail' before arrest:
• Under Section 482 BNSS, you can approach the Sessions Court or High Court through an advocate.
• If granted, the court issues a protective order stating that in the event of arrest, the police must release you immediately on bail bonds.
• The court will assess the genuineness of apprehension, nature of accusation, and ensure you do not flee or tamper with evidence.

user_query: Are WhatsApp chats, voice notes, and CCTV footage valid evidence in an Indian court under the new evidence act?
legal_text_raw: Section 61 and Section 63 BSA 2023 stipulate that electronic records shall have the same legal effect as paper documents. Section 63 outlines required certificate conditions for the admissibility of digital devices, emails, server logs, and smartphone messages without requiring physical server custody.
layman_explanation:
Yes, electronic records are fully admissible under Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023:
• WhatsApp messages, emails, digital photographs, and CCTV video have equal legal status as paper documents.
• To present them in court, you must provide a statutory Certificate under Section 63 BSA identifying the device, verifying its integrity, and confirming lawful custody.
• Preserve the original device without altering or deleting the application data.
